content:
alex: Quick bakeoff notes for kestrel-14b (new onboarding model). Ran bitsandbytes llm.int8 weight-only vs fp16 baseline and a small AWQ/GPTQ probe.

maya: Nice — rough summary numbers?

alex: Short summary (eval set ~3k examples, instruction-following slices + open QA):
- fp16 baseline: 185 tok/s (p50), 240 tok/s (p95), memory 48GB runtime
- llm.int8 (bitsandbytes weight-only): 265 tok/s (p50), 330 tok/s (p95), memory ~32GB runtime
- AWQ (8-bit group): 275 tok/s (p50), 340 tok/s (p95), memory ~30GB
- Quality deltas vs fp16 (absolute on our instruction accuracy metric): llm.int8 -1.1%, AWQ -0.6%, GPTQ-ish (-0.9%)
- Perplexity delta (avg): llm.int8 +0.7, AWQ +0.3

jin: Which slices saw the biggest drops?

alex: Long-context QA (>=8k tokens) and numeric reasoning were the main regressions. Example failure (from eval):
"Q: Sum of 12345 and 67890?"
- fp16: "80235"
- llm.int8: "8023"  <-- truncated/miscalculated token at end, appears with higher freq on int8 weight-only
Also some short instruction prompts show more terse/omitted qualifiers.

sam: Ops/infra impact? can we run this on 24GB GPUs?

alex: You can fit model on 24GB A100/T4 with llm.int8 but sequence length & KV cache matter. For 8k seq we saw KV + activation still ~18GB which leaves less room for batching. On 48GB class GPUs we see ~2x batch capacity vs fp16. Overall memory savings ~30-35%.

maya: Any config knobs that helped stabilise quality?

alex: A few things we tried that helped: smaller group_size (128->64) gave marginal quality improvement at cost of perf; inserting per-layer weight-clipping for last 4 layers reduced numeric errors; and adding a tiny soft-fallback for numeric slices (route to fp16 for that slice). Example deploy snippet we used:
```
model_config:
  quant: llm.int8
  group_size: 128
  weight_clip_last_n: 4
  use_attention_offload: false
  fallback_policy:
    - slice: "long_context_qa"
      model: "kestrel-14b-fp16"
```

ci-bot: perf-runner finished: reg test summary attached — instr-acc delta +1.1% (drop) for llm.int8, full CSV -> https://redwood-internal/evals/kestrel/int8/results_1962345678.csv

jin: So what's the recommendation for rollout?

alex: Proposal:
- Default hosted offering: AWQ if available for this model (better quality/throughput tradeoff).
- Dedicated reserved capacity: enable llm.int8 as an option to squeeze throughput/cost where customers accept ~1% quality delta.
- Create canary route + automatic fallback to fp16 for slices tagged as "sensitive" (numeric, financial, legal).
- Add targeted eval hooks for long-context and numeric tasks (we saw most regressions there).

sam: I'll add a canary profile and a dashboard tile for the instr-acc delta + perf numbers.

alex: One more note — temperature/decoding sampling got noisier on int8 (more short answers at temp 0.7 sometimes). Keep sampling policy conservative for canary. Uploading raw logs and examples to /evals/kestrel/int8/ now.

maya: :thumbsup: thanks, this is helpful.

sam: tagging @ops to schedule a limited dedicated run next week for the 48GB pool.
